title: Level 2: revision of the observation configuration and of its rules under scarce resources (confirmatory, DRAFT)
question: Does result-driven revision of the observation configuration (and revision of the revision rules) change what operations do afterwards, compared with no revision, with matched random revision and with revision without rule revision, under moderate scarcity of measurement resources?

hypotheses.text: Revising the controller's own rules changes later fired samples (C1; two-sided).
Result-driven revision changes later fired samples relative to no revision (C2; two-sided).
Result-driven revision differs from matched random revision (C3; secondary, underpowered: reported with its interval only).

arms.name: fixed-moderate
arms.description: History re-entry on, observation configuration never revised; moderately scarce measurement resources (0.5 per step).

arms.name: recursive-moderate
arms.description: The HPO-003 controller reconfigures the instruments from the reasons for blindness; moderate scarcity.

arms.name: recursive-meta-moderate
arms.description: As recursive-moderate; the controller's own rule parameters are revised (and rules exhausted) when a rule's change did not remove its blindness twice in a row.

arms.name: random-matched-moderate
arms.description: Random valid changes, the same number per epoch as recursive-moderate on the same seed.

notes: Functional template. Scarcity is imposed by settings.resources.pool_per_step; a revision of the rules, an exhausted rule or a stop is a record, not evidence of improvement or failure of any theory.

approval.note: REQUIRED and NOT GRANTED: about half a million step-runs; the researcher must approve before the protocol is created for running

status: DRAFT + PROPOSED AMENDMENT (known incomparabilities, numerical environment, one sensitivity analysis): not frozen, not run, not adopted; the original draft file is unchanged

preregistration.central_hypothesis: Under moderate scarcity, revising the observation configuration from the reasons operations were blind, and revising the controller's rules when they keep failing, changes the number of fired samples relative to the stated controls. No direction is assumed; equivalence is an equally valid result.
falsification: C1: the 95% interval of the paired difference in fired samples (recursive-meta vs recursive) lies inside +/-5% of the control mean: no detectable effect of rule revision
C2: the interval (recursive vs fixed) lies inside +/-20%: no detectable effect of result-driven revision of that size
any registered contrast whose interval includes zero and the margin is reported as unresolved, never as support

power.source: docs/level2/exploration_inputs/scarcity_functional_summary.json (functional run, 6 seeds, reserved range); upper 95% bound of each SD (chi-square, df 5)

sensitivity: leave-one-seed-out range of the mean difference
excluding runs that stopped early (censoring by stop.all_ceased)
analysis_plan.estimation: paired differences by seed; bootstrap 95% interval; Cohen's dz; sign-flip permutation p; Holm / BH over every declared contrast x metric

stopping_rules: per-run timeout 300 s, wall-clock budget 21600 s, at most 20 failed runs
no optional stopping: the number of seeds is fixed; a stopped study is resumed, never re-planned from partial results
preregistration.data_storage: every run record, the log, the manifest and the registered protocol are kept under the experiment directory; failed and timed-out runs are kept and counted

separation.confirmatory: the seeds of this protocol; disjoint from every exploratory and functional seed

known_incomparabilities: C2 (recursive vs fixed) compares policies that also differ in the instruments the controller sets over time: fired_samples are read through different instruments, so the contrast measures the policy together with the information it creates for itself, not the policy at equal information (declared: varies = controller, revision_authority).
random-matched matches the NUMBER of changes per epoch of the recursive arm, not their content or their resource cost: measure_cost can differ between arms and is a secondary metric, not a control.

stop.all_ceased ends a run early when every operation has ceased for an epoch: fired_samples of a stopped run accumulate over fewer steps. Arms with different stopping rates are compared conditionally on stopping; stopped_early and ceased_share are reported beside every contrast, and a sensitivity analysis excludes stopped runs (added to analysis_plan.sensitivity).
C3 is a secondary contrast declared underpowered (762 pairs needed against 200 planned): it is reported with its interval only and is not claimed as powered or as supporting anything.

the scarcity condition (pool_per_step 0.5, horizon 600) was chosen after looking at functional runs (provenance: exploration): the contrasts are conditional on that scarcity and say nothing about other levels of scarcity (the severe / none / abundant arms of the scarcity template are exploratory only).

the address hierarchy of the HPO world is a spectral split (method 1) whose result depends on the eigen-solver build (docs/RELIABILITY_REPAIR.md section 9; two known test failures): results are tied to the numerical build recorded in numerical_environment and are not claimed to reproduce bit-for-bit on another build.

the functional contrasts that sized this draft (6 seeds, reserved range) are not evidence: the stored sizing input gives C1 -4.83 (interval -14.5 to 0.0); an earlier status record quotes -26 for the first scarcity study; the two are not reconciled here, both are functional.

numerical_environment.hierarchy_method_note: the default spectral bisection; the opt-in method 2 (lod.hierarchy.build_hierarchy_v2) is NOT used and its results would not be mixed with method 1
